local_articles.snippet: s at Real Madrid. Vinicius scored in Brazil's opening 1-1 draw with Morocco and then also netted in the 3-0 defeat of Haiti. He is the first Brazilian to score in all three group matches at a World Cup since Ronaldo and Rivaldo both achieved the feat in 2002. The only other Brazilian players to find the net in all three group games are Jairzinho, in 1970, and Romario in 1994 -- that is illustrious company to keep, and Brazil went on to lift the trophy every time one of their players did that in the past. "I always say I am not that bothered about numbers. I am not used to scoring so many goals, but the coach has moved me into a position to which I have adapted well, and now I am scoring and helping the team," Vinicius told Brazilian broadcaster CazeTV.

The top two teams in each of the 12 groups, along with the eight best third-place finishers, advance to knockouts. The knockout phase begins with the round of 32, introduced for the first time at a World Cup after the expansion of the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. Then comes the round of 16, followed by the quarterfinals, semifinals and a playoff for third place. The final is on July 19. The stage-wise breakdown of the tournament’s schedule is: Group stage: June 11 to June 27 Round of 32: June 28 to July 3 Round of 16: July 4-7 Quarterfinals: July 9-11 Semifinals: July 14-15 Bronze medal match: July 18 Final: July 19 What are the rule changes for the tie-breaker criteria at the 2026 World Cup? questions.title: Who will be the first player to reach the men's singles final at Wimbledon in 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the winner of the first men's singles semifinal completed at the 2026 Wimbledon Championships, according to the tournament's official match results. Resolution Date : 2026-07-10 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: With Carlos Alcaraz ruled out of Wimbledon 2026 (wrist injury), defending champion and World No. 1 Jannik Sinner (~59% to win title, ~76% to reach the final) is heavily favored to win his half, while newly crowned Roland Garros champion Alexander Zverev moves up to No. 2 seed and is guaranteed the opposite half from Sinner (~23% to reach the final). Before the June 26 draw and July 9 semifinal order of play, each half has roughly a 50% chance of being scheduled first on Centre Court on July 10 (Wimbledon alternated top/bottom halves first across 2023-2025). Multiplying each contender's final-appearance probability by 0.50 yields calibrated marginal odds for winning the first completed semifinal, leaving ~25.5% for the rest of the field.

local_articles.title: Sinner's body and mind in focus for Wimbledon title defence
local_articles.snippet: Jannik Sinner will begin his Wimbledon title defence under close watch after his French Open stumble, with concern not just about what his body can endure but how physical disruptions can feed into a game that leaves little room for doubt. The warning signs surfaced in Paris, where Sinner's campaign ended in a physically compromised second-round defeat, prompting the Italian to return to Milan for medical tests as questions about the toll of a relentless season grew. Sinner has since adopted an unusual build-up to Wimbledon by skipping traditional grasscourt tune-up tournaments in favour of controlled training blocks, including work on hardcourts, as he prioritises regaining fitness and rhythm. questions.title: Who will win the women's singles title at Wimbledon in 2026?
questions.background: Wimbledon is one of tennis's four Grand Slam tournaments and is played on grass in London.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official Wimbledon results identifying the 2026 women's singles champion. Resolution Date : The question resolves when the tournament officially confirms the winner of the 2026 women's singles final. Accepted Answer Format : The winning player's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Consensus late-June 2026 betting markets (20Bet, Paddy Power, DraftKings) have World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka (~4.2-4.3 decimal) and 2022 Wimbledon / 2026 Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina (~5.0-5.2, managing a recent hip scare) as the top two favorites, followed by defending 2025 Wimbledon champion Iga Swiatek (~7.6-8.0, no WTA final since Sept 2025) and 2026 French Open champion Mirra Andreeva (~7.8-8.0). Power-law de-vigging of the high-overround 128-player WTA outright market and Wimbledon's historical parity (eight straight different champions since 2016) keep the top five summing to 58.5%, with ~41.5% on a deep field including Amanda Anisimova, Jessica Pegula, Linda Noskova, and Marta Kostyuk.

questions.title: Who will win the men's singles title at Wimbledon in 2026?
questions.background: Wimbledon is a Grand Slam tennis tournament played on grass courts in London.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The champion recorded in Wimbledon's official results for the 2026 men's singles tournament. Resolution Date : Resolve when the men's singles final, scheduled for July 12, 2026, is completed and the winner is officially confirmed. Accepted Answer Format : The winning player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Carlos Alcaraz's withdrawal with right-wrist tenosynovitis leaves defending 2025 Wimbledon champion and World No. 1 Jannik Sinner as an overwhelming favorite across June 23-24 bookmakers (1.40-1.61 decimal, de-vigging to ~59% after accounting for slight rust/fatigue risk following his Roland Garros retirement and lack of official grass tune-ups). Seven-time champion Novak Djokovic (5.55-6.00) and reigning 2026 French Open champion Alexander Zverev (8.0-11.0, seeded No. 2 opposite Sinner) lead the chase, with grass finalists Taylor Fritz (Stuttgart/Halle runner-up, withdrew precautionary from Eastbourne) and World No. 5 Ben Shelton (Stuttgart champion) rounding out the top five.

questions.title: Which country will win the 2026 ICC Women's T20 World Cup?
questions.background: The Women's T20 World Cup is the International Cricket Council's world championship for women's national teams in Twenty20 cricket.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official tournament final result published by the International Cricket Council, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Resolve when the winner of the 2026 tournament is established by the final's official result. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the winning country.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 24, Australia sit 4-0 (+4.724 NRR) in Group A after thrashing South Africa, Bangladesh, Netherlands, and Pakistan (by 113 runs), effectively locking up a semi-final berth as heavy favorites (~49%). Hosts England are unbeaten at 3-0 (+2.490 NRR) in Group B and nearly guaranteed a semi-final (~26% title probability). West Indies are also 3-0 (+0.644 NRR) with winless Ireland still to play (>90% semis), while South Africa (2-1, beat India) and India (2-1, +2.511 NRR, facing Bangladesh and Australia) battle for Group A's second spot, giving each roughly 8% title odds.

questions.title: Who will be named Player of the Tournament at the 2026 ICC Women's T20 World Cup?
questions.background: The Player of the Tournament award recognizes an individual player's performance across the competition.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The International Cricket Council's official announcement of the Player of the Tournament for the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup. Resolution Condition : Resolve when the recipient of the tournament-wide award is officially announced, rather than any individual match award. Accepted Answer Format : The recipient's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Women's T20 World Cup Player of the Tournament awards have gone exclusively to finalists since 2009 and to the champion in every edition since 2016, strongly favoring all-rounders on Australia (~49% to win) and England (~26%). Ellyse Perry already has two Player of the Match awards for unbeaten Australia (2-14 & 19* vs Bangladesh; 71 & 2-9 vs Pakistan), making her the clear individual frontrunner (18%), with teammate Georgia Wareham (POTM vs SA with 32 & 3/13, tournament-best 4.07 economy) also prominent. England's Nat Sciver-Brunt (SR 159) and Sophie Ecclestone (7 wickets) plus South Africa's Marizanne Kapp (81* & 2/27 vs India, 3/23 vs Pakistan) lead the chase, while ~50% probability remains across a wide field including Hayley Matthews, Smriti Mandhana, Sree Charani, Danni Wyatt-Hodge, and Sophie Molineux.

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Formula One British Grand Prix?
questions.background: The British Grand Prix is held at Silverstone as part of the Formula One World Championship.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The race classification published by Formula One or the FIA, corroborated by contemporaneous race reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the driver classified as the winner of the British Grand Prix scheduled for July 5, 2026. Sprint results do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning driver's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Mercedes has dominated early 2026 with 7/7 poles and 6/7 wins, led by championship leader Kimi Antonelli (5 consecutive wins before a late mechanical DNF from P2 in Barcelona). However, Toto Wolff flagged Mercedes reliability as their Achilles heel, and Ferrari just broke through with Lewis Hamilton winning Barcelona after back-to-back P2s in Canada and Monaco—plus Hamilton is a 9-time Silverstone winner. George Russell (3/7 poles including Barcelona) and home-race challenger Lando Norris (P3 Barcelona) also carry strong podium-to-win upside, with ~9% left on Piastri, Verstappen, and the field.

local_articles.title: Antonelli welcomes Mercedes upgrade as Russell says beware Hamilton
local_articles.snippet: Spielberg bei Knittelfeld – Formula One leader Kimi Antonelli said on June 25 that a Mercedes upgrade would help him bounce back from a first defeat of the year but teammate George Russell warned that Lewis Hamilton was back to his “beautiful best”. Russell, a 28-year-old Briton, was the pre-season favourite for the drivers’ title until his teenage Silver Arrows partner Antonelli reeled off a record run of five consecutive wins, a streak that Hamilton ended in Barcelona on June 14. It was Hamilton’s first victory for the “scarlet scuderia”, after two consecutive second places. He climbed to second in the title race, 41 points behind Antonelli, who retired in Spain, and nine ahead of Russell.
